title: How Photosynthesis Works
narrationPrompt: Write a 60-second spoken explainer for a vertical educational short called 'How Photosynthesis Works'. Use ten scenes, each about six seconds. Keep the voice direct, visual, and conversational. Explain that plants do not eat sunlight; they use light energy to rearrange water and carbon dioxide into sugar. Cover chlorophyll catching light, water splitting in the thylakoid membrane, oxygen leaving as waste, carbon dioxide entering through stomata, the Calvin cycle building glucose, and glucose storing energy for the plant and the food chain. Avoid dense jargon unless immediately explained. No stage directions, no markdown, no hashtags.
imagePromptRules: Full-frame single scene, no panels, no grid, no split-screen, no storyboard.
No text, no labels, no logos, no watermarks.
Show the mechanism literally with visible molecules, chloroplast structures, sunlight, leaf tissue, and soft educational motion cues.
Cinematic biology illustration, crisp edges, high contrast, luminous greens, gold sunlight, deep teal shadows, clean depth of field.
videoPromptRules: No camera cuts, no panels, no grid, no collage.
Subtle living-painting motion: drifting particles, flowing molecules, gentle camera push, pulsing light.
Preserve the composition, scientific clarity, and no-text rule.

scenes.caption: Plants do not eat sunlight. They use it like a battery charger.
scenes.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic scientific animation still of a healthy green leaf held against warm sunlight, seen close enough to reveal translucent veins and tiny glowing chloroplasts beneath the surface. Gold photons stream into the leaf like soft particles. The background is deep teal and forest-green, with shallow depth of field and luminous rim light. Full-frame single scene, no text, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, no panels, no grid.

scenes.caption: Inside each leaf cell, chloroplasts catch light with a green pigment called chlorophyll.
scenes.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 macro cutaway inside a leaf cell. Several oval chloroplasts float in clear cytoplasm, each filled with stacked thylakoid membranes that glow emerald and gold where sunlight lands. Chlorophyll is represented visually as green light-absorbing surfaces, not text. Scientific animated-video still, crisp biology illustration, no text, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, no panels, no grid.
scenes.videoPrompt: oval chloroplasts floating inside a leaf cell as thylakoid stacks pulse emerald and gold where sunlight touches them, with gentle cytoplasm motion

scenes.caption: That light energy splits water molecules into hydrogen, electrons, and oxygen.
scenes.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 close scientific illustration of water molecules arriving at a glowing thylakoid membrane inside a chloroplast. The water molecules separate into tiny bright electron sparks, pale hydrogen particles, and paired oxygen bubbles. The mechanism is clear and literal, with a dark teal cellular background and luminous gold-green energy. No text, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, no panels, no grid.

scenes.caption: The oxygen is not the goal. It is the leftover waste drifting out.

The stomata are visible as small openings in the leaf surface, and oxygen exits as clear blue-white bubbles into the air.
